backends.summary: HTTP JSON API: GET /api/v1/query_range, read as a matrix
HTTP JSON API: GET /api/traces, read as a list of traces whose spans carry hex ids
HTTP JSON API: GET /loki/api/v1/query_range, read as streams of [ns-timestamp, line] pairs whose service label the caller names

backends.reason: Elasticsearch returns hits under dynamic mappings, so the timestamp field, the message field and the service field are per-index decisions: the same query against two clusters yields two shapes, and a reader would need a field mapping supplied by the caller before it could read anything at all

the ClickHouse HTTP interface executes a SQL statement the caller writes and returns it in whichever format was asked for, so supporting it means either fixing a schema this project does not own or accepting arbitrary SQL -- the second of which would make the ingest path untyped

the Kubernetes API needs credentials that are not available to the ingest path -- an in-cluster service-account token or a kubeconfig -- and its events use the involvedObject vocabulary rather than the OTel resource attributes the IR is built on, so the reader would also need a translation table
